summary: Presentation/responsive pass at Desktop 1440x900, Tablet 768x1024 (portrait), Tablet 1024x768 (landscape) and Mobile 390x844 for /, /quick-order, /checkout (incl. guest-checkout form) and /my-library (admin signed in, 2FA skipped). No horizontal scrollbar detected on any page at any breakpoint (document.scrollWidth equals clientWidth at all 4 viewports x 4 pages). Confirmed the user-reported homepage hero compression on TABLET PORTRAIT (768): hero stacks vertically because Tailwind `lg:flex-row` only activates at ≥1024px, so at 768 the book cover drops below a tall column of headline+benefits+CTAs+denomination note+inclusion chips+Independence Day callout, leaving the book cover (~224px) floating alone in the lower section with large empty side margins — visually disconnected from the text. Tablet landscape (1024) and mobile (390) hero render well. Also found Quick Order ‘Small Group Options’ card is constrained by `max-w-xl` (576px) on a much wider parent on desktop/landscape — causing a large empty band on the right of the card.

ui_bugs.issue: At tablet portrait 768, hero stacks (col) because breakpoint is `lg:flex-row` (≥1024px). Stack order is headline -> 3 benefits -> CTAs -> denomination note -> Catholic/Protestant/Orthodox/Evangelical chips -> Independence Day callout -> ~600px of vertical space before the book cover (224px) sits centered with large empty space around it. Matches the user-reported 'compressed / stacking too tightly' complaint. The book cover feels disconnected from the message.

ui_bugs.component: Quick Order ‘Small Group Options’ card wrapper (QuickOrder.js line 968)
ui_bugs.issue: Card wrapped in `<div className="max-w-xl">` (576px) but parent section is ~960px wide on desktop and 1024 tablet landscape — leaves a large empty band on the right (~400px) making the section look unfinished/unbalanced. At 768 portrait the empty space is smaller but still noticeable.

ui_bugs.component: Checkout guest form ‘Your Items’ card @ mobile 390
ui_bugs.issue: Item row (name + qty selector + price + trash icon) packs tightly at 390 — the red `$9.99` and delete icon sit at the very right edge with `$9.99 each` overlap risk for longer product names. Quantity buttons (- 1 +) and price share one cramped row.

ui_bugs.component: Checkout coupon row @ tablet 768 single column
ui_bugs.issue: `COUPON OR GIFT CERTIFICATE` input + `Apply` button share one tight row; placeholder text gets visually truncated to 'CERTIFICATI' when Apply takes its share. Still functional but tight.

issues: Vertical stack is too long before the book cover appears (headline 3-line + 3 benefits + 2 CTAs + 3-line italic note + 4 chips + campaign callout, then cover)
Book cover floats alone in the lower band with large empty side gutters — feels detached from the message
Recommendation: switch breakpoint to `md:flex-row` (≥768px) so iPad portrait gets the two-column layout, or shorten the left column at ≤lg by hiding chips/denomination note in a collapsed form

Tiles wrap to 2x2 (sm:grid-cols-4 falls back to grid-cols-2 below sm). 'Foundation in Christ' / 'BOOKLETS AVAILABLE NOW' wraps to 2 lines while other tiles’ sub-labels are 1 line, creating uneven tile heights (cosmetic)

'Small Group Options' card is left-aligned and only ~576px wide on a 960–992px container, leaving a large empty band on the right. Either remove the `max-w-xl` wrapper, increase to `max-w-3xl`, or center the card on wider viewports.

Two-column layout collapses to single column at 768 (md:grid-cols-2 likely triggers at ≥1024 or has md gating). The grid stacks rather than going 2-up at iPad portrait — matches brief’s intent, no action needed.

action_items: PRIMARY: Fix homepage hero compression on tablet portrait. Change `flex flex-col lg:flex-row` to `flex flex-col md:flex-row` (SoulFoodApp.js line 571) so the iPad-portrait 768 breakpoint gets the two-column layout (text left, book right) instead of stacking. Also review `gap-8 lg:gap-14` -> `gap-6 md:gap-10 lg:gap-14`.

SECONDARY: In QuickOrder.js line 968, remove the `max-w-xl` wrapper around `<SmallGroupBundleCard />` or change to `max-w-3xl` so the Small Group Options card uses the available section width (especially on ≥1024). Optionally center it: `mx-auto`.
MINOR: At mobile 390 the Checkout 'Your Items' product row is tight; consider stacking qty controls under the title or shrinking the trash icon padding so the price doesn’t touch the edge.
OPTIONAL: Even-out July4 banner tile sub-label heights so 'BOOKLETS AVAILABLE NOW' (2 lines) doesn’t make Foundation tile taller than its neighbors.
critical_code_review_comments: Hero responsive breakpoint mismatch: the hero uses `lg:flex-row` (1024px) while almost every adjacent section already responds at `sm`/`md`. This is the single largest cause of the reported tablet-portrait compression.
QuickOrder.js wraps SmallGroupBundleCard in a hard `max-w-xl` which contradicts the section heading’s full-width treatment — causes visual whitespace imbalance on wider viewports.
No horizontal scroll anywhere — good. All cards/grids stack cleanly. Badges, headings, prices remain readable at all four viewports.
Login button selector ambiguity (tab 'Sign In' vs submit 'Sign In') made automation fragile. Adding `data-testid="login-submit-button"` on the auth form’s submit button would harden tests.

rca of the issue: RCA — Homepage hero tablet-portrait compression: SoulFoodApp.js line 571 uses `flex flex-col lg:flex-row`. Tailwind’s `lg` is 1024px, so at iPad-portrait 768 the layout stays in a column. The left column contains: 3-line headline, 3 numbered benefits, 2 CTAs, italic 4-line denomination note, 4 inclusion chips, and the Independence Day callout block — totaling ~900px tall. Only then does the right column (book cover 224px) appear. Result: visually the cover floats alone with empty side gutters, perceived as 'compressed/disconnected'. Reproduction: set viewport to 768x1024, navigate to /, scroll to y≈770, observe stacked hero. Mitigation: switch the breakpoint to `md:flex-row` (768) so iPad portrait splits into text|cover, mirroring the working 1024 landscape layout. Verified at 1024 landscape the same DOM renders correctly with two columns.
